items.headline: New Cabinet takes effect as PM Wong's reshuffle is sworn in
items.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's reshuffled Cabinet was sworn in on 27 July, with Jeffrey Siow promoted to Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance and David Neo to Minister for Culture, Community and Youth. The Ministry of Trade and Industry will be renamed the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry from 1 October.

items.headline: Ong Ye Kung warns over-servicing could make healthcare unaffordable
items.summary: At the Business Times Longevity Forum on 25 July, Health Minister Ong Ye Kung cautioned that over-servicing, unnecessary treatments and over-generous insurance riders risk driving up costs, warning that they create expense rather than health or wealth.

items.headline: Former entertainment lawyer Samuel Seow dies at 53
items.summary: Samuel Seow, founder and chief executive of talent agency Beam Artistes, died in his sleep on 25 July at age 53, with the attending doctor citing a heart attack, according to a family statement.

items.headline: Man, 48, hospitalised after group attack in a Yishun carpark
items.summary: A 48-year-old man was left unconscious and bloodied after being set upon by a group of five to six people in an open-air carpark in Yishun on 24 July; police are investigating.

items.headline: Singaporean man, 25, to be charged with murder over girlfriend's Bali death
items.summary: Muhammad Zulhelmi, 25, faces a murder charge after his girlfriend Angelica Suherman, 26, was found dead in a South Denpasar rental; an autopsy attributed her death to asphyxiation, and the case file was sent to Denpasar prosecutors.

items.headline: Update: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns over NEET paper-leak protests
items.summary: Dharmendra Pradhan quit the Union cabinet on 25 July after weeks of nationwide student protests over the NEET-UG paper leak that forced a retest affecting around 2 million students; President Droupadi Murmu accepted the resignation.

items.headline: BJP veteran Pralhad Joshi handed additional charge of Education Ministry
items.summary: On 26 July, Consumer Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the Education Ministry, a day after Pradhan's resignation, and is expected to oversee promised National Testing Agency exam reforms.

items.headline: India's markets shrug off student protests as the rupee nears a record low
items.summary: Indian equities have stayed steady through the student unrest, but the rupee weakened about 0.3% this week toward a record low, driven largely by a renewed surge in crude prices; the Reserve Bank of India intervened to support the currency.

items.headline: India presses China on market access and courts a US trade deal at Manila
items.summary: On the sidelines of the ASEAN meetings in Manila on 22 July, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar pushed his Chinese counterpart on market access and trade balance, and joined US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in urging an interim India-US trade agreement despite Trump's pharmaceutical-tariff threat.

items.headline: Burnham rules out an early election and vows to 'call out' Trump
items.summary: In his first major interview as prime minister, Andy Burnham ruled out calling a snap general election before the 2029 due date, insisting his government is legitimate, and said he would be prepared to stand up to Donald Trump to defend UK interests despite a warm first exchange.

items.headline: Burnham's cabinet more exposed to Reform than Starmer's, polling finds
items.summary: New modelling suggests only six members of Andy Burnham's cabinet would keep their seats if an election were held now, with 12 losing to Nigel Farage's poll-leading Reform UK and four to other parties.

items.headline: Thames Water creditors pitch a 'golden share' to avert nationalisation
items.summary: Senior creditors of Thames Water, whose debts approach £20 billion and which could run out of money by October, offered ministers a 'golden share' to head off Burnham's push to take the 16-million-customer utility into temporary public ownership.

items.headline: Farage and Reform under scrutiny over crypto-billionaire funding
items.summary: Nigel Farage faces questions over an undisclosed £5 million gift from Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, plus some £25 million given to Reform UK, ahead of the Clacton by-election triggered by his resignation.

items.headline: Berlin Pride car-ramming suspect shot dead by police after manhunt
items.summary: A van drove into Christopher Street Day crowds in Berlin's Tiergarten on 25 July, killing one woman and injuring 29; the 21-year-old German-Lebanese suspect was shot dead by police on 26 July after a nearly 24-hour manhunt in what the interior minister called an Islamist terror attack.

items.headline: Typhoon Noul makes landfall in southern China as hundreds of thousands flee
items.summary: Typhoon Noul, the strongest storm to hit China in 2026, struck Guangdong's Huizhou early on 26 July; more than 340,000 people were relocated and over 1,000 flights were cancelled across Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Hong Kong.

items.headline: Iran accuses Ukraine of a deadly strike on a Caspian Sea vessel
items.summary: Iran said a Ukrainian attack on an Iranian commercial ship in the Caspian Sea killed one sailor and summoned Kyiv's envoy on 26 July; President Zelenskyy said Ukrainian strikes hit vessels carrying Iranian military cargo, while Tehran called it a UN Charter violation.

items.headline: Drone strikes on a Kazakh oil terminal push Tokayev to urge a truce
items.summary: Repeated drone strikes on tankers at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's Black Sea terminal, which handles about 80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports, forced a suspension of shipments; sitting beside Vladimir Putin on 25 July, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said it might be 'time to freeze this conflict.'

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5, its fourth Claude 5 model in two months
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on 24 July with a one-million-token context window and pricing held at $5 and $25 per million input and output tokens; the company says it approaches its flagship Fable 5's performance at roughly half the cost.

items.headline: Tech industry urges against broad restrictions on open-weight AI models
items.summary: Twenty-five US technology companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta and Hugging Face, signed a 24 July letter urging policymakers to avoid 'premature restrictions' on open-weight AI models as Washington weighs its response to advanced Chinese systems; signatories reportedly neared 50 within a day.

items.headline: Alphabet's Anthropic stake valued at about $124bn in an SEC filing
items.summary: Alphabet disclosed in a 23 July filing that its private-company investments, primarily its roughly 14% stake in Anthropic, were worth about $124 billion as of 30 June, booking nearly $77 billion in unrealised second-quarter gains ahead of Anthropic's targeted October IPO.

items.headline: Robotics startup Genesis in talks to raise at a $3bn valuation
items.summary: Genesis AI is in talks to raise about $500 million at a $3 billion pre-money valuation, with Premji Invest reportedly in discussions to lead, a sharp jump from its $105 million seed round a year earlier.

items.headline: US stock futures rally ahead of megacap earnings and the Fed meeting
items.summary: US futures jumped on 26 July, with Dow futures up about 294 points (0.6%), S&P 500 futures up 0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures up 1.2%, as oil eased on a weekend pause in US-Iran fighting and traders braced for megacap earnings and the 29 July Fed decision.

items.headline: CME launches single-stock futures on more than 50 big US companies
items.summary: CME Group begins trading single-stock futures on 27 July, with 55 standard and 22 micro contracts covering names such as Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Nvidia and SpaceX, giving traders leveraged, cash-settled exposure without options.

items.headline: Fed rate-hike odds surge toward 47% ahead of the 29 July meeting
items.summary: With rates at 3.50%-3.75%, CME FedWatch put the chance of a 25-basis-point hike at about 46.5%, up from under 12% a week earlier, as a surge in oil prices stoked inflation fears before the 29 July FOMC decision.

items.headline: Bain and LY weigh a higher bid for Japan's Kakaku to rival EQT
items.summary: Bain Capital and LY Corp. are considering a fresh joint takeover offer for Japanese online marketplace Kakaku.com, likely above the roughly 3,450-yen-per-share bid EQT made a week earlier, escalating a bidding war for the operator of restaurant site Tabelog.

items.headline: 🏎️ Norris wins a dramatic Hungarian GP as Piastri retires from the lead
items.summary: Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen by about 15 seconds to win the Hungarian Grand Prix for his first victory of 2026, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli third; McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri retired from the lead with a gearbox failure on lap 56.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli keeps his title lead despite Norris's Hungary breakthrough
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli's third place at the Hungaroring kept him atop the 2026 drivers' standings, though race-winner Lando Norris and runner-up Max Verstappen both closed the gap heading into the summer break.

items.headline: 🏏 India complete a 3-0 T20I sweep of Zimbabwe in Harare
items.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struck 81 off 49 balls to power India to 192 for 5, and Mayank Yadav's 3 for 29 helped restrict Zimbabwe as India won the third Twenty20 international by 35 runs to complete a clean series sweep.

items.headline: 🎾 Teenager Lilli Tagger wins the Prague Open for her first WTA title
items.summary: The 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger beat Ukraine's Daria Snigur 7-6(3), 6-2 in the Prague Open final to capture her maiden WTA Tour singles title.

items.headline: 🎾 Korpatsch beats Bondar to win the Hamburg Open on home clay
items.summary: Germany's Tamara Korpatsch defeated Hungary's Anna Bondar 6-3, 6-3 in the final of the Hamburg Open to lift her second WTA Tour singles title.

items.headline: Alzheimer's 'tipping point' in brain immune cells may decide who develops dementia
items.summary: Analysing brain tissue from older people with and without dementia and from cognitively intact centenarians, researchers identified an amyloid-to-tau inflection point at which microglia switch states; resilient centenarians activated protective gene programs, pointing to microglia as a therapeutic target.

items.headline: A giant 'exosatellite' around a brown dwarf challenges what counts as a moon
items.summary: Astronomers used radial-velocity spectra to detect a companion of at least about 0.7 Jupiter masses orbiting the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 B, 73 light-years away; because the object is planet-sized yet orbits another substellar body, researchers dispute whether it is the first true exomoon.

items.headline: Study estimates humans spoke up to ten times as many languages 2,000 years ago
items.summary: A study in Science led by Damian Blasi estimates linguistic diversity peaked at roughly 20,000 to 75,000 languages about 2,000 years ago, some ten times today's total, before a sharp decline the authors link to the spread of large empires rather than later European colonialism.

items.headline: A 1,900-year-old Roman latrine helps explain why Roman concrete lasts millennia
items.summary: Analysis of ancient inland Roman concrete confirmed calcite as a key binding phase and showed directly how it holds the material together, helping explain the exceptional durability of Roman structures and pointing toward longer-lasting modern cements.

items.headline: The thymus, a 'forgotten' organ, may help control inflammation as we age
items.summary: New research indicates the small thymus gland plays an outsized role in regulating age-related inflammation and, demonstrated in mice, could be leveraged to extend healthy lifespan, reframing an organ long thought to become vestigial in adulthood.

fun_fact.headline: It rains diamonds inside Uranus and Neptune
fun_fact.body: Deep inside the ice-giant planets Uranus and Neptune, pressures above a million atmospheres are thought to crush carbon out of methane and squeeze it into diamonds that sink toward the core — a literal rain of diamonds. Laboratory experiments at SLAC, which fired lasers at plastic to mimic those conditions, have actually produced tiny diamonds this way, and a 2024 study suggests the process spans a far larger region of the planets than once believed.

puzzle.title: Turn the Triangle
puzzle.body:
Ten coins sit in a triangle pointing UP, four rows tall:

        ●
       ● ●
      ● ● ●
     ● ● ● ●

Moving exactly THREE coins, make the whole triangle point DOWN instead. Which three coins do you move?
puzzle.approach: Think about which coins are shared between an upward triangle and a downward one, then move only the coins that are not.
puzzle.answer:
Move the three 'corner' coins.

The upward and downward triangles share the same middle seven coins, so seven stay exactly where they are. Move the single top coin down to become the new bottom tip, and move the two bottom-corner coins up to sit on either side of the old apex, forming the new four-coin top row. The result is an identical triangle pointing down — done in three moves.

word_puzzle.title: Cross Purposes
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into four groups of four:

DUCK · SERVE · FOLD · CREASE
ACE · OVER · RAISE · TEAR
MAIDEN · FAULT · SCORE · CALL
BOUNCER · RALLY · PRESS · BLUFF
word_puzzle.approach: Each word looks like it could join more than one group. Find the single home where all four members share a precise link, and watch for the deliberate traps.
word_puzzle.answer:
TENNIS: SERVE, ACE, FAULT, RALLY
POKER (betting actions): BLUFF, RAISE, FOLD, CALL
ACTIONS ON PAPER: CREASE, TEAR, PRESS, SCORE
CRICKET: OVER, DUCK, BOUNCER, MAIDEN

Traps: FOLD looks like a paper action but is a poker move; CREASE and SCORE look like cricket terms but are things you do to paper; ACE could be a playing card but is a tennis shot; RALLY could be motor racing but is tennis.
